ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is quadrilateral ABCD, A is at the lower left, B is on the left side, C is above, D is at the lower right; diagonal AC has been drawn. The figure marks ∠ABC = 75°, ∠BCA = 30°, ∠CAD = 50°, and what is required is the angle at point D, ∠ADC. The problem also gives BC = AD. Reasoning: In triangle ABC, ∠BAC = 180° - 75° - 30° = 75°. Therefore ∠BAC = ∠ABC = 75°, so the sides opposite them are equal, namely BC = AC. Also because the problem gives BC = AD, so AC = AD. Thus triangle ACD is an isosceles triangle, and the vertex angle ∠CAD = 50°, therefore the two base angles ∠ACD and ∠ADC are equal. Thus ∠ADC = (180° - 50°) / 2 = 65°.

raw_record.question_text: Some angles in the quadrilateral $ABCD$ are shown in the figure. If $BC=AD$, then what is the angle $ADC$?

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as quadrilateral ABCD with diagonal AC drawn. The shown angles are ∠ABC = 75°, ∠BCA = 30°, ∠CAD = 50°, and the unknown is ∠ADC. From the text, use BC = AD. First work in triangle ABC: ∠BAC = 180° − 75° − 30° = 75°, so ∠BAC = ∠ABC. Therefore the opposite sides are equal, giving BC = AC. Combine this with the text condition BC = AD to get AC = AD. Then triangle ACD is isosceles with vertex angle ∠CAD = 50°, so its two base angles are equal: ∠ACD = ∠ADC = (180° − 50°)/2 = 65°.

method.method_draft: Read from the figure that triangle ABC has ∠ABC = 75° and ∠BCA = 30°, triangle ACD has ∠CAD = 50°, and the requested angle is x = ∠ADC. Read from the text that BC = AD. In triangle ABC, compute ∠BAC = 180° − 75° − 30° = 75°. By the sine rule in triangle ABC, BC/AC = sin(75°)/sin(75°) = 1. Since AD = BC, this gives AD/AC = 1. Now apply the sine rule in triangle ACD: with x = ∠ADC, the third angle is ∠ACD = 180° − 50° − x = 130° − x, so AD/AC = sin(130° − x)/sin x. Set this ratio equal to 1, giving sin(130° − x) = sin x. In the valid angle range for triangle ACD, this yields 130° − x = x, so x = 65°.
